# stack-selection

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D2 Architecture & System Design (AR)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** MADR template and guidance — https://adr.github.io/madr/ ; Twelve-Factor config and portability constraints — https://12factor.net/config
- **Depends on:** requirements-writing, system-design
- **Feeds into:** adr-writing, system-design

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** choosing or replacing a language, framework, database, queue, or any component the project will depend on for its lifetime; re-evaluating a settled stack decision.
- **Do NOT use when:** the component is already settled by an accepted ADR and nothing material has changed (build on it), or the choice is a leaf utility inside one module with no architectural reach (decide locally, note it in the pull request).

## Rules

1. **AR-041 — Criteria before candidates.** The selection criteria are written down before any candidate is named: requirements fit, data-model fit, team skill, ecosystem maturity and maintenance health, license, operational cost, hosting constraints, exit cost.
2. **AR-042 — Same table for every candidate.** Each candidate is scored against the same criteria in one comparison table. A candidate evaluated on criteria the others were spared is re-evaluated.
3. **AR-043 — Every adoption is an ADR.** No stack component is adopted without an ADR in MADR format whose status is "accepted", naming at least one seriously considered alternative and why it lost.
4. **AR-044 — Popularity is not a criterion.** "Popular", "trending", and "used at a big company" never appear as selection criteria or as a candidate's scored advantage.
5. **AR-045 — Versions agree everywhere.** Versions named in the ADR, the README stack list, and any prose must match the dependency manifest exactly. A mismatch is a defect.
6. **AR-046 — Pin in the same change.** Exact versions are pinned in the dependency manifest in the same change that adopts the component; "install latest" is not a pin.
7. **AR-047 — Disqualifiers are recorded.** A candidate with no maintenance activity, a license conflict with the project's license, or no production hosting path on the target platform is disqualified, and the disqualification is written in the ADR — not silently dropped from the table.
8. **AR-048 — Downsides are accepted on record.** The ADR states the chosen component's accepted downsides (the criteria where it scored worst). An ADR claiming no downsides is incomplete.
9. **AR-049 — Exit cost is assessed.** For data stores and platforms, the ADR states what leaving would cost: data export path, proprietary features in use, and contract or ecosystem lock-in.
10. **AR-050 — Changes supersede, never swap silently.** Replacing a settled component requires a new ADR that supersedes the old one and links both ways. Editing the manifest alone is forbidden.

## BAN list

- **BAN-AR-021 — Fashion adoption.** Banned: adopting a component because it is fashionable, with no criteria table and no ADR. Defeats: DET-CODE-024. Instead: write the criteria, score at least two candidates in one table, and record the choice as an ADR (AR-041, AR-043). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AR-022 — Version drift between prose and manifest.** Banned: a version named in the README or ADR that differs from the dependency manifest. Defeats: DET-CODE-028. Instead: the manifest is the single source; prose is regenerated or corrected to match it (AR-045). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AR-023 — The silent swap.** Banned: replacing a settled stack component by editing the manifest, with no superseding ADR. Defeats: DET-CODE-032. Instead: a new ADR supersedes the old one, links both ways, and lands in the same change (AR-050). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AR-024 — The unmaintained dependency.** Banned: adopting a component with no maintenance activity or an unresolved license conflict without recording the risk. Defeats: DET-INF-025. Instead: disqualify it in the ADR with the reason recorded, or accept the risk explicitly with a mitigation (AR-047). Severity: WARN.

## Gates

- **G-AR-021 — Manifest-to-ADR coverage (citation).** Verifies: AR-043. Check: automated — this requirement is verified by the canonical manifest cross-check, G-AR-122 in adr-writing (every top-level manifest dependency maps to an ADR by name or tag match); run that gate for the full procedure and pass criteria. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AR-022 — Version agreement.** Verifies: AR-045, AR-046. Check: automated — a script extracts version strings from the README stack list and the ADRs and compares them with the manifest's pinned versions. Pass: zero mismatches and zero unpinned top-level dependencies. Fail: block merge. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AR-023 — Criteria predates decision.** Verifies: AR-041, AR-042, AR-048. Check: manual — in git history, confirm the criteria table exists at or before the commit that records the decision, the table scores every candidate on the same criteria, and the ADR names a rejected alternative and accepted downsides. Pass: all three hold. Fail: block stack sign-off. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- Criteria first, candidates second — always in that order.
- No ADR with a rejected alternative, no adoption.
- Popularity is not a criterion.
- The manifest is the only version that counts.
- A swap without a superseding ADR is a silent swap.

## Checklist

- [ ] Criteria were written before candidates were named (AR-041).
- [ ] Every candidate is scored in one table against the same criteria (AR-042).
- [ ] The ADR is accepted, names a rejected alternative, and states accepted downsides (AR-043, AR-048).
- [ ] Manifest-to-ADR coverage is 100% (G-AR-021).
- [ ] Versions in prose match the manifest exactly; everything is pinned (G-AR-022).
- [ ] Disqualified candidates are recorded with their disqualifier (AR-047).
- [ ] Exit cost is stated for stores and platforms (AR-049).

<!-- generated from skills/architecture/system-design/SKILL.md (bundle form) -->

# system-design

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D2 Architecture & System Design (AR)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** C4 model — https://c4model.com/ ; Pattern language for distributed designs — https://microservices.io/
- **Depends on:** requirements-writing, stack-selection
- **Feeds into:** c4-diagrams, adr-writing, data-architecture

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** a new system or a major subsystem is being designed; the container topology, data ownership, or failure behavior of an existing system is being changed; a design review is requested.
- **Do NOT use when:** the change fits inside one existing container without new cross-boundary calls (build it and update the diagram via c4-diagrams instead), or when the open question is which stack to build on (stack-selection comes first).

## Rules

1. **AR-001 — Containers are real.** Every container in the design corresponds to a deployable unit, data store, or external system that exists in the repo or infrastructure config. Aspirational boxes are deleted or marked as future work outside the diagram.
2. **AR-002 — Every arrow is labeled.** Each relationship between containers carries a protocol or format label (HTTPS/JSON, gRPC, AMQP, SQL). An unlabeled arrow fails review.
3. **AR-003 — Failure behavior per call.** For every cross-container call, the design states the timeout, the retry policy, and what the caller does when the callee is down. A call missing any of the three is incomplete.
4. **AR-004 — Monolith by default.** The default topology is a modular monolith. A distributed design must cite, in an ADR, the requirement that forces it (independent scaling, team autonomy, isolation) — "future scale" without a load figure does not qualify.
5. **AR-005 — One writer per store.** Each data store has exactly one owning container that writes to it. Other containers read through the owner's interface or a replicated read model, never by writing directly.
6. **AR-006 — Quality attributes first.** Decomposition starts from the stated quality attributes (scale, latency, consistency, availability, tenancy), each with a target figure where one exists. A design that names components before attributes is sent back.
7. **AR-007 — Failure in the same pass.** Timeouts, retries, backpressure, and degradation are designed in the same pass as the happy path for every flow, not retrofitted after the first outage.
8. **AR-008 — Decisions become ADRs when made.** Each significant choice in the design (topology, ownership, protocol, consistency model) gets an ADR at the moment it is made, not reconstructed at the end of the project.
9. **AR-009 — Revisit on attribute change.** The design is revisited when a quality attribute changes (a new tenancy requirement, a 10× load target), not on a calendar schedule. The triggering change is named in the review note.
10. **AR-010 — External systems are explicit.** Every external system on the diagram is named, with the direction of the integration, whether it is synchronous or asynchronous, and who owns the relationship.

## BAN list

- **BAN-AR-001 — The generic three-box diagram.** Banned: a design whose whole model is boxes labeled "Frontend", "Backend", "Database" with unlabeled arrows. Defeats: DET-CODE-008. Instead: a C4 container diagram with typed elements, named protocols on every arrow, and data stores as first-class containers (AR-001, AR-002). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AR-002 — Aspirational containers.** Banned: containers in the design that exist in no deployable unit, data store, or infrastructure config. Defeats: DET-INF-024. Instead: draw what exists; put the recommendations box in a clearly marked future-work note outside the diagram. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AR-003 — Distribution without a forcing requirement.** Banned: splitting the system into services with no ADR citing the requirement that forces distribution. Defeats: DET-CODE-015. Instead: a modular monolith with module boundaries, plus an ADR naming the load or isolation figure that would trigger a split (AR-004). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AR-004 — Shared writable database.** Banned: two or more containers writing directly to the same tables. Defeats: DET-CODE-030. Instead: one owning writer; the other container calls the owner's interface or consumes its events (AR-005). Severity: WARN.

## Gates

- **G-AR-001 — Container-to-deployable walk.** Verifies: AR-001, AR-010. Check: manual — walk the container diagram element by element against the repo's deployable units and infrastructure config; every element must match a real unit, store, or named external system, and every relationship line in the diagram source must carry a protocol label (checked here, by eye, because label syntax differs across diagram formats). Pass: zero unmatched elements and zero unlabeled relationships. Fail: block design approval. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AR-002 — Design document completeness.** Verifies: AR-002, AR-008. Check: automated — a script confirms ARCHITECTURE.md contains a container section and that every ADR file it references exists under `docs/decisions/`. Pass: script exits 0. Fail: block design approval. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AR-003 — Failure-behavior review.** Verifies: AR-003, AR-007. Check: manual — for each cross-container call in the design, point at the row stating its timeout, retry policy, and callee-down behavior. Pass: every call has all three. Fail: block design approval. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AR-004 — Data-ownership audit.** Verifies: AR-005. Check: manual — list every store in the design and its owning writer; confirm no second container writes to it directly. Pass: exactly one writer per store. Fail: block design approval. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- Start from quality attributes, not components.
- Every container is real; every arrow is labeled.
- Timeout, retry, callee-down — for every call.
- Monolith by default; distribution needs a forcing requirement.
- One writer per store, always.

## Checklist

- [ ] Every container matches a deployable unit, store, or named external system (G-AR-001).
- [ ] Every arrow carries a protocol or format label (AR-002).
- [ ] Every cross-container call states timeout, retry policy, and callee-down behavior (G-AR-003).
- [ ] Data ownership is drawn: exactly one writer per store (G-AR-004).
- [ ] A distributed topology, if any, cites its forcing requirement in an ADR (AR-004).
- [ ] Each significant decision has an ADR written when it was made (AR-008).
- [ ] External systems are named with direction and sync/async marked (AR-010).
